3:1.sourceText: Ταύτην ἤδη, ἀγαπητοί, δευτέραν ὑμῖν γράφω ἐπιστολήν, ἐν αἷς διεγείρω ὑμῶν ἐν ὑπομνήσει τὴν εἰλικρινῆ διάνοιαν,
3:1.targetText: This [is] now, beloved, a second letter I write to you, in both which I stir up your pure mind in reminding [you]

groups.note: The actual letter recipients you are also the people whose mind the letter stirs by a reminder. English resumes those same stated addressees as bracketed [you] after reminding, without a separately written second Greek recipient pronoun.

The actual in-which plural relative resumes the letters, with second identifying the two-letter sequence. English clarifies that plural two-letter reference as in both which; it does not claim an independently written Greek both quantifier.

unmappedSource.reason: Greek article has no separate English word in this noun phrase.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies a copular frame for this-second-letter statement; the actual Greek writes this ... second letter I write, without a corresponding be verb.

3:2.sourceText: μνησθῆναι τῶν προειρημένων ῥημάτων ὑπὸ τῶν ἁγίων προφητῶν καὶ τῆς τῶν ἀποστόλων ὑμῶν ἐντολῆς τοῦ Κυρίου καὶ Σωτῆρος,
3:2.targetText: to be mindful of the sayings said before by the holy prophets, and of the command of us the apostles of the LORD and Savior,

groups.note: The actual genitive article/apostles phrase gives the command’s apostolic relationship. English states the apostles apposition after of us; the differing first/second-person possessor is separately explained, without making a sole article mean of.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual N1904 pronoun is second-person plural your, ὑμῶν, qualifying apostles; LSV has first-person us. The unlike personal relationship is not equated.

unmappedTarget.reason: LSV gives first-person us the apostles where pinned N1904 writes your apostles with second-person ὑμῶν.

3:3.sourceText: τοῦτο πρῶτον γινώσκοντες, ὅτι ἐλεύσονται ἐπ’ ἐσχάτων τῶν ἡμερῶν ἐν ἐμπαιγμονῇ ἐμπαῖκται κατὰ τὰς ἰδίας ἐπιθυμίας αὐτῶν πορευόμενοι
3:3.targetText: knowing this first, that there will come scoffers in the last days, going on according to their own desires,

groups.note: The actual own adjective and personal possessor jointly identify the same desires belonging to the scoffers. English condenses this actual double possessive into their own, without dropping either identity.

unmappedSource.reason: N1904 explicitly includes in mockery/scoffing, ἐν ἐμπαιγμονῇ, alongside the actual scoffers noun. LSV omits this additional manner phrase; the distinct mocking-act noun is not silently relabeled as the actor noun.
Greek article has no separate English word in this noun phrase.

3:4.sourceText: καὶ λέγοντες Ποῦ ἐστιν ἡ ἐπαγγελία τῆς παρουσίας αὐτοῦ; ἀφ’ ἧς γὰρ οἱ πατέρες ἐκοιμήθησαν, πάντα οὕτως διαμένει ἀπ’ ἀρχῆς κτίσεως.
3:4.targetText: and saying, “Where is the promise of His coming? For since the fathers fell asleep, all things so remain from the beginning of the creation”;

3:5.sourceText: λανθάνει γὰρ αὐτοὺς τοῦτο θέλοντας ὅτι οὐρανοὶ ἦσαν ἔκπαλαι καὶ γῆ ἐξ ὕδατος καὶ δι’ ὕδατος συνεστῶσα τῷ τοῦ Θεοῦ λόγῳ,
3:5.targetText: for this they willingly conceal, that the heavens existed long ago, and the earth having been established by the word of God out of water and through water,

groups.note: The actual willing participle qualifies the people whose notice the fact escapes; English states their willingness adverbially. The separate conceal/nonnotice agency difference is explained rather than treating this volition word as proof of an active hiding verb.

The actual perfect active intransitive συνεστῶσα denotes the earth standing constituted/formed. LSV presents that same constituted state passively as having been established; the source is not changed into a Greek passive participle or a different founding verb.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual λανθάνει with accusative them says this escapes their notice/is hidden from their notice, while they are willing. LSV instead makes them agents of concealing. This nonnotice versus active-concealment predicate/participant difference is not forced into an exact head match.

unmappedTarget.reason: LSV makes these people the active concealing subject; the actual Greek αὐτούς marks those whose notice the fact escapes, not the subject of a conceal verb.
LSV gives active conceal, while pinned N1904 writes λανθάνει, escapes notice, with the fact as subject and them as experiencers. No unstated conceal-from-themselves interpretation is invented.

3:6.sourceText: δι’ ὧν ὁ τότε κόσμος ὕδατι κατακλυσθεὶς ἀπώλετο·
3:6.targetText: through which the world then, having been flooded by water, was destroyed;

3:7.sourceText: οἱ δὲ νῦν οὐρανοὶ καὶ ἡ γῆ τῷ αὐτῷ λόγῳ τεθησαυρισμένοι εἰσὶν πυρὶ τηρούμενοι εἰς ἡμέραν κρίσεως καὶ ἀπωλείας τῶν ἀσεβῶν ἀνθρώπων.
3:7.targetText: and by the same word, the present heavens and earth, having been stored up for fire, are being preserved until [the] day of judgment and destruction of impious men.

unmappedSource.reason: Greek article has no separate English word in this noun phrase.

3:8.sourceText: Ἓν δὲ τοῦτο μὴ λανθανέτω ὑμᾶς, ἀγαπητοί, ὅτι μία ἡμέρα παρὰ Κυρίῳ ὡς χίλια ἔτη καὶ χίλια ἔτη ὡς ἡμέρα μία.
3:8.targetText: And do not let this one thing be concealed from you, beloved, that one day with the LORD [is] as one thousand years and one thousand years as one day;

groups.note: The actual third-person imperative with accusative you means let this not escape your notice. English states the same fact/nonnotice-experiencer relation as do not let it be concealed from you; the full idiom supplies that English passive/from relation without inventing a separate Greek concealing agent or from preposition.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies a copula in the day/thousand-years comparison; no corresponding Greek be verb is written.

3:9.sourceText: οὐ βραδύνει Κύριος τῆς ἐπαγγελίας, ὥς τινες βραδύτητα ἡγοῦνται, ἀλλὰ μακροθυμεῖ εἰς ὑμᾶς, μὴ βουλόμενός τινας ἀπολέσθαι ἀλλὰ πάντας εἰς μετάνοιαν χωρῆσαι.
3:9.targetText: the LORD is not slow in regard to the promise, as some count slowness, but is long-suffering to us, not intending any to be lost, but all to come to conversion,

groups.note: The actual genitive promise phrase is the concern/complement of the delaying predicate. English expands that case-governed relation as in regard to the promise; regard is not an independently written Greek noun or verb.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual N1904 pronoun is second-person plural you, ὑμᾶς, while LSV has first-person us. The different written recipients are not equated.

unmappedTarget.reason: LSV gives us where pinned N1904 writes you, ὑμᾶς. The actual patience predicate and its goal preposition remain linked independently.

3:10.sourceText: Ἥξει δὲ ἡμέρα Κυρίου ὡς κλέπτης, ἐν ᾗ οἱ οὐρανοὶ ῥοιζηδὸν παρελεύσονται, στοιχεῖα δὲ καυσούμενα λυθήσεται, καὶ γῆ καὶ τὰ ἐν αὐτῇ ἔργα εὑρεθήσεται.
3:10.targetText: and it will come—the Day of the LORD—as a thief in the night, in which the heavens will pass away with a rushing noise, and the elements will be dissolved with burning heat, and [the] earth and the works in it will not be found.

groups.note: The actual καυσόω burning participle gives the elements’ burning condition, nominalized in English as with burning heat. Its whole heat/burning expression belongs to this actual predicate, not a separately written Greek heat noun or with preposition.

The actual N1904 εὑρεθήσεται is the positive future passive will be found. LSV adds not, separately explained as a source-witness negation difference; no Greek negative is fabricated and the verb is not relabeled burned.

unmappedTarget.reason: The night-location phrase is additional wording in LSV, absent from pinned N1904.
LSV negates the final found predicate, while pinned N1904 has positive εὑρεθήσεται without a written negative. The opposite assertion is kept visible rather than silently merging the readings.

review.note: The actual installed LSV text says will not be found, not burned up. The actual installed N1904 text says will be found without the negative. Only the shared finding predicate is paired, with the extra English negation left unpaired and the original assertion preserved.

3:11.sourceText: Τούτων οὕτως πάντων λυομένων ποταποὺς δεῖ ὑπάρχειν ὑμᾶς ἐν ἁγίαις ἀναστροφαῖς καὶ εὐσεβείαις,
3:11.targetText: All these, then, being dissolved, what kind of persons ought you to be in holy behaviors and pious acts,

groups.note: The actual genitive-absolute these/all/being-dissolved construction supplies this whole dissolution circumstance, rendered by the English plural subject plus participle rather than independently changing the Greek case.

The actual plural godliness/piety noun denotes manifestations of piety; English renders it pious acts. Its adjective/act support belongs to that one real nominal designation, not separate original pious and act words.

unmappedSource.reason: N1904 has οὕτως, thus/in this manner, describing the dissolution; LSV gives inferential then. The distinct manner/conclusion words are not treated as an exact lexical identity.

unmappedTarget.reason: LSV gives inferential then where pinned N1904 has the manner word οὕτως, thus/in this way.

3:12.sourceText: προσδοκῶντας καὶ σπεύδοντας τὴν παρουσίαν τῆς τοῦ Θεοῦ ἡμέρας, δι’ ἣν οὐρανοὶ πυρούμενοι λυθήσονται καὶ στοιχεῖα καυσούμενα τήκεται·
3:12.targetText: waiting for and hurrying the coming of the Day of God, by which the heavens, being on fire, will be dissolved, and the elements will melt with burning heat?

groups.note: The actual burning participle gives the elements’ condition, rendered by the English manner/heat phrase with burning heat. No independent original with preposition or heat noun is claimed.

N1904 uses the present singular middle/passive τήκεται, is melting/being melted, with a neuter-plural elements subject. English narrates future will melt; the actual melting head is retained with that tense/voice/number presentation explicit.

3:13.sourceText: καινοὺς δὲ οὐρανοὺς καὶ γῆν καινὴν κατὰ τὸ ἐπάγγελμα αὐτοῦ προσδοκῶμεν, ἐν οἷς δικαιοσύνη κατοικεῖ.
3:13.targetText: And we wait for new heavens and a new earth according to His promise, in which righteousness dwells;

unmappedSource.reason: Greek article has no separate English word in this noun phrase.

3:14.sourceText: Διό, ἀγαπητοί, ταῦτα προσδοκῶντες σπουδάσατε ἄσπιλοι καὶ ἀμώμητοι αὐτῷ εὑρεθῆναι ἐν εἰρήνῃ,
3:14.targetText: for this reason, beloved, waiting for these things, be diligent, spotless and unblameable, to be found by Him in peace,

3:15.sourceText: καὶ τὴν τοῦ Κυρίου ἡμῶν μακροθυμίαν σωτηρίαν ἡγεῖσθε, καθὼς καὶ ὁ ἀγαπητὸς ἡμῶν ἀδελφὸς Παῦλος κατὰ τὴν δοθεῖσαν αὐτῷ σοφίαν ἔγραψεν ὑμῖν,
3:15.targetText: and count the long-suffering of our Lord [as] salvation, according as also our beloved brother Paul—according to the wisdom given to him—wrote to you,

groups.note: The actual salvation accusative is the predicative complement of count/consider. English expresses that actual object-complement role as as salvation, not an independently written Greek as preposition.

unmappedSource.reason: Greek article has no separate English word in this noun phrase.

3:16.sourceText: ὡς καὶ ἐν πάσαις ἐπιστολαῖς λαλῶν ἐν αὐταῖς περὶ τούτων, ἐν αἷς ἐστιν δυσνόητά τινα, ἃ οἱ ἀμαθεῖς καὶ ἀστήρικτοι στρεβλοῦσιν ὡς καὶ τὰς λοιπὰς γραφὰς πρὸς τὴν ἰδίαν αὐτῶν ἀπώλειαν.
3:16.targetText: as also in all the letters, speaking in them concerning these things, among which are some things [that are] hard to be understood, which the untaught and unstable twist, as also the other Writings, to their own destruction.

unmappedSource.reason: Greek article has no separate English word in this noun phrase.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies a relative/copular frame to paraphrase the nominal hard-to-understand-things adjective phrase. The actual Greek ἐστιν already supplies the earlier existential are; no second copula or relative pronoun is written here.

3:17.sourceText: Ὑμεῖς οὖν, ἀγαπητοί, προγινώσκοντες φυλάσσεσθε ἵνα μὴ τῇ τῶν ἀθέσμων πλάνῃ συναπαχθέντες ἐκπέσητε τοῦ ἰδίου στηριγμοῦ,
3:17.targetText: You, then, beloved, knowing before, take heed, lest, together with the error of the impious being led away, you may fall from your own steadfastness,

groups.note: The actual substantival lawless/unprincipled adjective ἀθέσμων names the offenders; LSV uses impious. The source keeps that lawless head, not a substituted ἀσεβής adjective.

unmappedSource.reason: Greek article has no separate English word in this noun phrase.

3:18.sourceText: αὐξάνετε δὲ ἐν χάριτι καὶ γνώσει τοῦ Κυρίου ἡμῶν καὶ Σωτῆρος Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ. αὐτῷ ἡ δόξα καὶ νῦν καὶ εἰς ἡμέραν αἰῶνος.
3:18.targetText: and increase in grace, and in the knowledge of our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ; to Him [is] the glory both now, and to the day of the age! Amen.

groups.note: The actual ἐν governs both coordinated grace and knowledge domains. English repeats in with knowledge; both retain that genuinely shared source preposition.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies a copula in the honor/glory doxology; no corresponding Greek be verb is written.
The final Amen is additional LSV source-witness wording; pinned N1904 ends with age without this word.
